title: LLMs for mobile engineers, from tokens to your app
intro: What actually happens when your app calls a language model: tokens, one at a time; why answers stream; why the model remembers nothing; why the same question gets different answers; where the API key must never live; and when the model should run on the phone instead. One small puzzle at a time.
how: Each puzzle starts with something you'll hit when you put a model in an app, gives you one building block, shows it in a diagram that plays itself, and ends with three questions you have to answer to unlock the next one. Facts come from Anthropic's and Android's documentation and Google Cloud's security guidance, linked on every page.
heroAlt: Animated diagram: a prompt becomes tokens; the model predicts one token, adds it, and predicts the next.

assumes.title: Mobile system design, from a packet to an app

modules.title: Module 1: A model in your app
modules.blurb: Tokens, streaming, statelessness and the context window, temperature, keys, and on-device models.

modules.title: Module 2: Text retrieval and evidence
modules.blurb: Compare two ways to find text, and test selection separately from the claims an assistant makes.

upcoming.title: Next: what a call costs and how it fails
upcoming.topics: max_tokens and a cut-off answer, why output tokens cost more than input, rate limits and retries, prompt caching, and structured output you can parse.

upcoming.title: Module 3: Tool use and chat assistants
upcoming.topics: Compare model tool calling and reusable skills with the same text cases. Under explicit permissions, connect a chat interface to a read-only test tool and inspect the tool logs.

upcoming.title: Module 4: Shipping it
upcoming.topics: Prompt caching and cost, evaluating answers, guardrails, latency budgets on mobile, and fallbacks when the model is down.
